sentences.text: The range of the tide follows the moon.
At new and full moon, the sun and moon line up and you get spring tides, with the biggest range.
Spring has nothing to do with the season.
At the first and third quarter moons, the sun and moon pull at right angles and you get neap tides, with the smallest range.
When a spring tide coincides with the moon’s closest approach to the earth, perigean spring tides, often called king tides, flood low-lying Florida streets.
Strong onshore winds and low pressure raise water levels, and offshore winds lower them.
